input.spec:
Audit pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/793 (branch cohort/task-lineage-composites/ba9a7e) in repository oakridge. This is an isolated verification run of the committed development definition, not feature work: its only purpose is real analysis, plan, brief, build_result and assessment artifacts for observation to capture and grade. The analysis reports at least three separate findings about this spec, each a distinct observation. Produce exactly one cohort, named audit, with two tasks. T1: a declaration is journaled only after its exact tasks revision is approved, and never steps the core (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/analysis-link-declaration.ts, oakridge-dbos/src/storage/commit.ts). T2: a composite selects the current revision per unit before reading links, and keeps stages apart (observation/src/grading/composite.ts, observation/src/storage/grading-record-store.ts).
The operator authorizes this audit path: the builder publishes the existing PR #793 as its pr artifact instead of pushing or opening one. No brief may add a further operator choice or confirmation. The builder must not edit files, create commits, push, open or update any pull request, merge, reset a database or deploy. Its worktree starts from epic/grade-pray, the base of pull request #793, so it first checks out the head of branch cohort/task-lineage-composites/ba9a7e locally (git checkout --detach origin/cohort/task-lineage-composites/ba9a7e) and inspects that commit, runs bun install if needed and then bun run --filter observation test once, and publishes build_result with the commit it inspected as head_sha and the actual test counts and output. A test that cannot run is a known issue, never a reason to invent results. It then publishes the existing pull request https://github.com/RankOneLabs/oakridge/pull/793 as the pr artifact, with branch cohort/task-lineage-composites/ba9a7e.
The assessor assesses that same commit without changing anything. Give at least one finding per task. Every finding cites at least one file as path:start-end at that commit, for example observation/src/grading/composite.ts:20-40, and cites test output separately as test or output evidence. Report the builder's test run as test_evidence.
Keep the spec, tasks, plan and brief short; there are no ambiguous requirements to resolve.

body.summary: The audit is implementable with no blocking decision and the requested one-cohort/two-task shape is supported by the repository. At c03533340ab94eb521315a29d0e76a9219c9b906, T1 validates the exact approved tasks revision before directly journaling a declaration without invoking the core, while T2 computes current standing per unit/artifact stream before associating links and derives independent stage composites from one snapshot. Two non-blocking spec corrections are recommended before planning: update the stale claim that the current epic/grade-pray checkout is the PR base, and add direct T1 test execution because the mandated observation workspace command does not run oakridge-dbos tests.

findings.description: T1 has a named domain model and exact-address approval gate: AnalysisLinkDeclaration carries run_id, tasks_revision_id, and typed entries, and selectDeclarationRefusal rejects a missing, wrong-artifact, or unapproved exact tasks revision before checking source findings (oakridge-dbos/src/domain/analysis-link-declaration.ts:10-22,43-53). The transaction queries approval against declaration.tasks_revision_id and refuses before insertion when that exact target lacks approval (oakridge-dbos/src/storage/commit.ts:770-785).

T1's no-core-step claim is directly auditable: commitAnalysisLinkDeclaration accepts only a database and declaration request, locks the run, checks replay and authority, and inserts authority.event plus a receipt without a CoreClient dependency or step call (oakridge-dbos/src/storage/commit.ts:731-785). Direct tests verify exact-revision refusal/acceptance and unchanged units, effect intents, and operator notices (oakridge-dbos/tests/analysis-link-declaration.test.ts:90-120,154-162).

T2 selects current revisions independently per [unit_id, artifact_kind] stream, resolves predecessor heads before timestamp fallback, and only afterward associates occurrences with relations (observation/src/grading/composite.ts:107-155). Tests cover per-unit heads, predecessor precedence, artifact isolation, and one cohort revision not hiding another unit's current revision (observation/tests/composite.test.ts:95-120,220-236).

T2 keeps stages separate: the public model exposes stages side by side with no cross-stage figure, and stageComposite filters linked contributions by stage before selecting current items and answers (observation/src/grading/composite.ts:274-303,314-372). The storage adapter reads revisions, occurrences, relations, executions, and answers under one tenant snapshot before invoking the pure selector (observation/src/storage/grading-record-store.ts:27-75); integration coverage checks implementation and integration answers remain distinct (observation/tests/composite.test.ts:238-260).

The required builder command runs only observation/package.json's bun test ./tests script, while T1's direct exact-approval/no-core tests live in oakridge-dbos and are classified as integration tests (observation/package.json:6-8, oakridge-dbos/tests/run-suite.sh:12-20, oakridge-dbos/tests/analysis-link-declaration.test.ts:90-120). Consequently, the mandated build_result output can directly exercise T2 but cannot honestly be cited as execution evidence for T1; add a targeted T1 run and report it separately, with inability to run remaining a known issue.

The checkout premise is stale in the current repository: origin/epic/grade-pray resolves to merge commit a8856584aaaa44017ac1de2cdc710876b1fbb706, whose subject is Deliver explicit analysis links and derive task composites (#793); audited branch head c03533340ab94eb521315a29d0e76a9219c9b906 is its ancestor, and both commits have tree 56d52e141a6e20343c1ae5d387e96d0809c22af0. The detach instruction still reaches the requested commit, but epic/grade-pray is no longer the base of PR #793 and the spec should not describe it as such.
